newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU REVIEWS EXPIRY OF IMPORT DUTY ON BRAZIL SILICON.
newsitem.headline: EU REVIEWS EXPIRY OF IMPORT DUTY ON BRAZIL SILICON.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it would review the European Union's anti-dumping duty on imports of silicon metal from Brazil, in effect postponing an earlier plan to let the duty expire.
The EU executive said in February that the anti-dumping duty, imposed in 1992, would expire on August 9 unless a review was initiated.

In a notice published in the EU's August 8 Official Journal, the Commission said it had agreed to a request from the Liaison Committee of the ferro-alloy industry (Euroalliages) to conduct such a review.
"The request is based on the grounds that the expiry of the measures would be likely to result in the recurrence of dumping, thereby causing injury to the Community industry," the Commission said.
It said this likelihood was supported by evidence of increased production capacity in Brazil adding to existing spare capacity, indicating the existence of an oversupply.

"It is further alleged that any surplus production in Brazil is most likely to be directed to the Community market due to a lower than expected increase in demand and strong competition on the other major markets for silicon metal and the effect of the anti-dumping measures recently imposed on Brazilian imports into the United States."

The request also alleged that an increase of Brazilian exports at dumped prices, combined with lower than forecast EU market growth, would lead to "severe price erosion, a reduction of production, sales and market share, as well as unsustainable financial losses threatening the very existence of the Community industry."

The Commission said it had determined that sufficient evidence existed to initiate a review and that it would seek information from EU producers, exporters and importers. They have 40 days to present their views.
Silicon is used to make primary and secondary aluminium.
